# Reviewer application

**Stellar Discovery Trust Layer — TokenJunkieLabs — SCF #46 Build / Open Track**

## Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs builds open-source, self-hostable software that carries a paid API, dataset or agent operation through to completed customer work. A merchant publishes an authorized resource; a buyer approves the exact request and total spending, pays through Stellar, and receives the complete result in its application. The merchant retains the offer, fulfillment and accounting. Another engineer can restore the installation and continue its original work.

We request **$38,000 for 400 prospective development and technical integration hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance**. The funded outcome is **two independently operated merchant services used by two independent buyer operators**:

* **Day 30:** both services installed with their authorized sources and accountable operators; one approved testnet purchase per merchant delivers the complete agreed output into its buyer's application.
* **Day 90:** at least ten useful testnet purchases in total across the two independent buyers during seven consecutive days, with both merchants represented; one selected merchant service operates through two independent facilitators with the same source, schema and useful output.
* **Day 150:** both merchants live on mainnet, with at least thirty useful purchases in total across the two independent buyers during fourteen consecutive days, both buyers returning on another UTC day, and completed recovery and independent maintainer handover.

The working product supplies the architecture, payments and source-to-customer foundation. The six packages below fund the selected installations' remaining source adapters, receiving integration, deployment, monitoring and recovery. Reusable improvements return to the public product; completed pre-award work remains the starting point.

## Customer problem, need and adoption

Our initial users are recurring API/data-service operators and the agencies integrating their services into customer applications. The commissioning payer buys implementation and handover; the merchant earns resource receipts; the independent buyer purchases useful output. These roles may belong to different organizations.

A paid response must become a usable customer result: every required page or file, the correct population and period, original units and types, and an output that opens in the receiving application. An interrupted request also needs a clear financial and delivery outcome. These requirements are especially important when an agent makes several paid requests to complete one task.

We support two recurring installation patterns:

|Customer task|Accepted output|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Receive a new economic or operational reporting period, then compare it with the previous edition.|Complete report and underlying selection, retaining units, periods, source editions and review decisions.|
|Run an approved typed query or acquire a refreshed dataset.|Every agreed page/file, with the exact request, source selection, aggregate cost and merchant record.|


The two funded installations and agreements remain to be selected. Current conversations refine the customer and payer model. CoCart’s founder asked how introductions, implementation fees, contracting and platform support would work; our October 12 proposal assigns introductions to CoCart, implementation and handover to TokenJunkieLabs under a direct customer contract, and a written referral arrangement. Veridex invited our existing buyer CLI into its testnet cohort and reported no third-party testing budget. Our latest reply proposes a paid buyer-integration pilot, partner funding or a specifically valued reciprocal workshare with agreed deliverables and usage rights. Blockscout expressed interest and reported no integration budget; Nansen declined. The [detailed customer and commercial plan](./product-and-finance.md#1-customer-problem-and-commercial-model) carries the corresponding installation roles and workshare scope.

Each selected workorder will name the payer, source owner, merchant, independent buyer, integration and receiving engineers, host and acceptance owner. It will specify the authorized population/period/query, useful output, advertised paid unit, aggregate spending limit and responsibility for hosting and purchases. An installed baseline and a later genuinely needed period, edition or query establish recurring demand. Source permission, operator availability and the complete customer task are settled before its deployed work begins.

The delivered economic, Timescale, aid-data and scientific-array applications provide concrete candidates for these two patterns. Existing proposed workshares retain their original source, effort, fees and customer conditions in the detailed application. For example, the GeoRobotix observation-source proposal is **$9,600 / 72 engineering hours / twelve active business days**, with two $4,800 milestones. Its first offer was sent on October 13 at 00:05:31 UTC; delivery starts after source selection, access and the receiving environment are ready. Its reusable illustrative-source workflow has completed review, query/export, separate receiving and cold reopen. The commercial case has separately completed scope planning, independent receiving and the maintained Installation intake; its eight engineering workorders remain planned. Customer installation, live collection and the paid Stellar service remain prospective.

The environmental commissioning programme makes that selection practical. Five original offers cover complete laboratory reissues, a client import, a monitoring study and a KiWIS programme. Their retained plans contain **25 phases /206 planned commercial hours /$24,600 in proposed implementation fees**, with $12,300 at agreed starts and $12,300 at accepted handovers. Those are sent proposals; no customer acceptance or revenue is recorded for this cohort. Four shipped Installation profiles translate the original scopes into source selection, scientific review, full output and independent receiving. Two laboratories share one technical profile while preserving separate case, plan and acceptance identities. The [installed operating course](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/6d18ad532aef87aad8982da1ff3c3426655ae014/stellar/scf_2026/sf49_data_commissioning/installation-workorders/ENVIRONMENTAL_INSTALLATIONS.md) lets the engineer open each original workshare, agree the customer’s actual source and receiving environment, and select a later useful delivery or reporting window. The two grant-funded installations remain independently selected.

The first-customer qualification now follows three named channels. [GeoRobotix](https://georobotix.com/services/) offers sensor-data platforms and integration APIs; its proposed task is a complete authorised observation period received by an independent analyst. [Lutra Consulting](https://www.lutraconsulting.co.uk/migration-to-open-source-gis) supplies QGIS migration and integration; its existing $8,000 /60-hour proposal covers a baseline and corrected vector edition. Its published HighWater and FLO-2D relationships provide possible introductions for a later dataset or model-input service. [Inspry](https://www.inspry.com/wordpress-services/javascript-frameworks/) supplies headless WooCommerce development and already has our separate $8,400 /56-hour offer for one store and digital product. CoCart's platform relationship and the commissioning agency can support that installation while the actual merchant owns fulfilment.

These source-qualified channels guide selection of the two services. A fixed migration or an agency introduction becomes a recurring paid-service candidate only when the actual buyer names its next useful period, query or order and agrees the source, paid unit and receiving result. The proposed pre-award course resolves those choices, available engineers and remaining adaptations by November 4, then carries the actual decisions into the invited submission for the published November 8 deadline. Customer research and sales remain outside the 400 funded hours. The [complete customer launch plan](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/b5cc37b64b180cc3740ceba37786aac68ff43a63/products/merchant-workspace/CUSTOMER_LAUNCH.md) connects each original Workshare to the existing Installation and Customer-use Calendar, the same six packages, native purchases, complete output and independent handover.

The purchase target follows actual work. Two buyers making one purchase per weekday would produce only twenty purchases in fourteen days. The chosen T3 work must therefore require at least thirty distinct useful paid requests across both buyers and merchants. Advertised pages can be separate purchases within one complete task; replay, reopening and cached use retain the original purchase. The existing Customer-use Calendar links the saved Installation, buyers, complete tasks and funding groups to the original purchase observations.

TokenJunkieLabs earns separately agreed implementation and care fees. Merchants retain resource revenue and implementation partners retain customer relationships. Each adaptation, delivery hour and support obligation is allocated once between the grant and commissioned work.

## Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar gives this product a shared authorization and settlement layer. In the existing x402 Exact flow, a buyer signs authorization for a particular payer, recipient, token amount and expiry, and a facilitator verifies and submits it on the selected network. Explicit fee sponsorship can cover submission costs. We use existing Stellar SDKs and token contracts. Our Open Track proposal is an application-level improvement: keeping a complete customer task usable from the reviewed request and spending decision through delivery, recovery and independent maintenance. The requested track remains subject to the issuer's invitation and review.

The buyer's useful unit of work can be larger than one paid response. An analyst may need every page in a selected dataset and an editable report; a service operator may need recurring results, their original source context and a handover another engineer can resume. A transport receipt alone does not specify whether that agreed task is complete. Our implementation retains the exact HTTP request or MCP tool and arguments, selected source edition, payment terms, aggregate approval, original operations and all agreed outputs together. Buyers retain signing and spending authority; merchants retain source-access, pricing and fulfillment authority.

|Existing foundation|Documented technical and business role|Our application-level contribution|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|Stellar x402 libraries and facilitators|Standard payment challenges, signed authorization, verification and settlement let merchants charge for resources using existing Stellar infrastructure.|Retain the concrete request, selected terms and total task approval with the original transfer and complete customer result, including tasks spanning multiple separately paid responses.|
|Stellar MPP SDK|Charge uses an on-chain transfer for each payment. Channel uses a funded Soroban channel and off-chain cumulative commitments, with later settlement. These are upstream payment capabilities.|The maintained MPP workspace carries selected service/task authority, original purchases and responses, collection, funding and recovery into an editable handover. Channel commitments remain distinct from on-chain transfers and from our historical purchase count.|
|ApiCharge|Its documented route grants retain purchased service levels, explicit limits and pricing terms, supporting paid access to a merchant's service.|Carry the selected access terms into the customer's complete source/query, output and later work, while retaining the original purchased allowance and consumption when defaults change.|
|MPP Router|Its documented Stellar-funded proxy provides paid access, request-ID response caching and authenticated asynchronous job polling.|Keep the reviewed request contents, source and payment selection bound to the original operation across interrupted delivery, complete output collection and independently received editable workspaces.|


The table places each provider's documented payment or access capability alongside our implemented customer workflow. The technical contribution is the retained relationship across the whole task. Its business value is continuity for the customer and the next operator: they can inspect what was approved and paid, distinguish a pending payment from incomplete delivery, and continue the original work after an interruption or handover.

The completed team-operated evidence includes a 144-row HPD task delivered in two pages of 100 and 44 rows, with two distinct 10,000-stroop payments. A separate original MySQL purchase returned 100 rows and 14 columns with its actual truncation flag; its complete response and purchase history reopened in another directory with signing disabled. These establish working pagination, paid-result retention and receiving in those particular team-operated testnet cases. The historical baseline remains 18 distinct team-operated testnet purchases totaling 411,000 stroops, with fees separate. Source checks, analytical runs and Channel commitments retain their separate classifications.

The six funded packages turn that foundation into two independently operated merchant installations and two buyers. Each first-tranche installation must complete an approved native Stellar testnet purchase and useful output. The two-facilitator comparison then holds the useful service, schema, source population and output constant; the retained Vellar/Periplo catalogue comparison found no shared seller/route identity, so registration and integration of that same service remain funded work. Later acceptance measures the already-defined recurring-use cohorts and both merchants' mainnet operation. Reusable source/consumer, deployment and receiving improvements return to the public product. Delivery remains within the original $38,000 request, 400 prospective hours, 150 days and six package commitments.

Primary documentation: [Stellar x402](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/agentic-payments/x402/built-on-stellar), [Stellar MPP SDK](https://github.com/stellar/stellar-mpp-sdk), [ApiCharge](https://apicharge.com/Documentation/core-concepts.html) and [MPP Router](https://www.mpprouter.dev/llms.txt). The substantive comparison and operating evidence are included in this answer.

## Defined architecture and operating behavior

The architecture is defined and implemented across six components:

|Component|Responsibility|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|**Merchant workspace**|Select authorized source/query, schema, output, price and limits. Retain separately reviewed source and terms changes or withdrawal.|
|**HTTP or MCP resource**|Preserve types, nulls, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live semantics. Use customer-controlled source credential references.|
|**Buyer approval and budget**|Approve exact method/tool, arguments, scope and payment option; match the challenge and schema before signing. Reserve aggregate task spending alongside per-payment limits.|
|**Stellar settlement**|Use the reviewed network, asset, recipient, amount, expiry and fee policy. Reconcile the native transfer through independent RPC observation.|
|**Delivery and accounting**|Retain all agreed outputs, original attempts, accepted fulfillment, notifications and acknowledgments. Preserve prepaid selection/consumption, usage periods, prices, invoices and receipts.|
|**Recovery and receiving**|Keep approval, settlement and delivery states distinct; reconcile the original dispatch after an uncertain response. Restore source, configuration, history and files for another authorized engineer.|


Catalog browsing retains the full selected page, offer and payment alternative. Advertised schemas guide explicit request inputs; the saved intent contains the concrete request, body and spending limit. The Request Collections input library accepts original catalogue and body files from desktop or phone, resumes interrupted transfers, and retains exact inputs privately. Buyers select the actual offer and advertised terms, then use saved plans and named periods through the existing review and spending controls. Recovery and downloads reopen that same service workspace. A prepaid call retains its selected pass and consumed allowance when defaults change. MPP Charge and the implemented Channel workspace retain their distinct approval and recovery lifecycles. Channel tasks bind the selected contract, service and spending authority to original commitments, responses and later collection; commitments remain distinct from on-chain transfers and the historical testnet purchase count. The maintained Runtime Applications file library carries the customer's complete original file into its reviewed application configuration, retaining a separate editable working copy and the original upload through backup and receiving. A saved Runtime procedure carries the named task, operating decisions, full selected source, files and revision history to the next engineer. The customer-delivery workspace then packages the complete retained responses and selected application source for independent receiving.

The [prepaid commissioning desk](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/0bc8fc4b6b83efb7c20833e431bdb6233279d178/products/prepaid-api/COMMISSIONING.md) carries that installation work from reviewed checkout, payment, allowance and host settings to the original native preparation, generated source and Applications setup document. The merchant retains its publication; the customer receives the complete handoff and opens the original workspace. A portable editable document carries those exact results and configuration history to the next engineer. This shipped commissioning source supports the first thirty days of installation work; its executed authored source course adds no purchase or independent buyer to the development baseline.

The [complete financial walkthrough](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/main/stellar-forge/developer-site/dist/grant-data/financial-walkthrough.md) continues the original merchant and customer from the useful paid result through quote/invoice review, actual Stellar or bank receiving, dated allocations, refunds, bank reconciliation and customer close. Its browser, HTTP, CLI and 46 receivables MCP actions share the original accounting workspace. Customer/order setup, usage captures, reviewed service periods, saved closing cycles, corrections and complete handovers retain their own records. Purchase principal, fees, commercial valuation, separately issued obligations and later service activity keep their respective identities.

The [merchant invoice-intake programme](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/1d91db51af1b721ab979907ae3739fcacc965200/products/x402api-merchant-workspace/INVOICE_INTAKE.md) takes complete CSV or JSON source through reviewed mapping and invoice creation across the browser, HTTP API, typed client and CLI. It preserves the original source, stable invoice IDs and frozen recipient, asset, amount and expiry terms. An interrupted preparation reopens its complete original request; a partial creation resumes against the original invoices. The full invoice register and portable customer handover carry this same source and history into the next operator’s installation. These shipped capabilities support the first thirty-day commissioning package.

Node.js supplies browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces; source and receiving applications also use Python/SQLite and PHP/WordPress/WooCommerce. Each facilitator has explicit network, asset, recipient, signer and fee policies. T2 configures two compatible testnet operators for the same service; T3 deploys each merchant's reviewed mainnet configuration. Existing SDKs/contracts remain the payment foundation. The selected x402 Exact integration uses existing Stellar token contracts. Its public release identifies the upstream contract and SDK source, versions and licenses alongside the maintained integration code; any funded modifications to contract code will be included under compatible open-source terms. The existing [unified development guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/68929767fd9c138e3bcee2df65ea9e5928ca565a/products/merchant-workspace/DEVELOPMENT.md) collects the architecture and diagram, interface ownership, roadmap, development artifacts and native acceptance/recovery plan. The application states the technical design and acceptance outcomes here; that guide supplies the full development material.

**Named delivery and financial operation.** The existing Grant Operations workspace gives lead, finance, reviewer and contributor staff individual sign-ins and assigned cases. Work, invoices, observed payments and corrections retain their original records and named actors; the complete installation carries those records and source into independent restoration.

## Working product and demonstrated results

The working product demonstrates three customer outcomes. Its development baseline is **18 distinct team-operated testnet purchases totaling 411,000 stroops / 0.0411 native XLM**, with fees separate. Independent customer deployments and mainnet use are the funded next stage.

**Complete recurring dataset receiving.** All **830 original OData Orders** passed through typed collection, saved SQL, a report, a two-sheet workbook and independent analytical receiving. Three subscription editions, original-request replay, independent publisher/customer restores and restored-publisher continuation completed. The same source definition produced zero row changes, retained as the actual result. The separate managed selection built and loaded all twelve entry points; managed preparation/adoption and Review → Start → receive → Stop → reopen remain to be operated on that completed customer edition.

**A real Stellar purchase with a useful output.** Two 10,000-stroop purchases completed one **144-row Queens HPD customer task**, received as pages of 100 and 44 rows and reopened as CSV/JSONL with original source and accounting. A separate 50,000-stroop purchase returned 100 rows and fourteen columns, retained its original truncation flag, and reopened with signing disconnected and in another directory. Reviewers can inspect the [original acquisition record](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/687ea12ac97f06b7f1336676249c349ade7a7692/products/merchant-workspace/DEVELOPMENT.md#5-existing-delivery-foundation-and-receiving-examples), [reviewer operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/03a93f7c59a703ebc63416ae0e914f07099fef37/products/grant-reviewer/OPERATING.md) and [3:32 product/team film](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/releases/download/scf-presentation-20261011/stellar-forge-scf46-presentation.mp4).

**Completed merchant financial receiving.** The original authenticated merchant HTTP/MCP lifecycle completed eight workflows on October 13: sealed quotation and response recovery after source aliases changed, reviewed USD 100 invoice issue, retained wallet observation and cancellation, a USD 25 credit with the corrected USD 75 receipt, complete customer files, interrupted-download recovery and cold reopening with zero due. Its paired invoice-wallet programme completed seven workflows for exact native/issued-asset amounts, fee-bump aliases, request replay and testnet/commercial separation. The [retained native results](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/2c69f99e2a787a0ff4966e1029c809fc65a8c0c2/operations/scf-receivables-native-2a51-20261012/HOSTED_RECEIVING.md) identify source 94ad1dd3 and the three exact startup corrections. They use official SDK-generated transaction/result XDR and controlled RPC observations; the original network-purchase register remains the basis for paid-use totals.

**Independent restoration and handover.** The OData receiver restored and continued the original subscription. [Saved prepaid passes](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/24506172ed7c4288d158ab7f6c1735c645dc6ab9/operations/api-pass-portfolio-agent-921ba0-20261012/NATIVE_RESULT.json) preserved each call’s selected pass and consumed allowance through replay and cold receiving. The [OpenLineage customer operation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/1b1f756587619d21cab44f627f5d4e9b4fa6ad72/products/openlineage/OPERATING.md) let another engineer reopen accepted measurements, reports and history. Installation, recurring requests, bank statements and customer service closing retain their original operating and financial records. The complete Resource Review operation also received a conflicting reviewer return, applied the reviewed resolution, exported its full journal and continued editing after independent receiving without the original source files. Twelve desktop and phone views completed with no recorded page or console errors. Its [merged customer continuation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/835) connects the Python entry, exact comparison and originating return to that full review.

Discovery also has a measured baseline against the actual 27-resource Vellar testnet catalog: schema-aware ranking retrieved all 31 declared query-resource relationships versus 22 previously, with matching direct/indexed results across 33 queries. The [complete comparison](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/main/stellar-forge/developer-site/dist/grant-data/catalog-parameter-evaluation-20261012.json) retains that source-based measurement.

The merged [IATI operating-procedure component](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/0110a7fde307112abee5be63a06291855aa72599/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/iati/document_evidence/OPERATING_PROCEDURES.md) adds editable customer plans and complete analyst receiving. The [detailed product companion](./product-and-finance.md) preserves the full product inventory, source populations, operating outcomes and remaining deployment steps. Selected customer source/roles, deployed purchasing/recovery and production handover remain within the existing T1, T2 and T3 packages.

The Human Services Directory has also completed its original native source-to-referral and independent receiving operation: twenty mapped fields, three resulting FHIR resources, retained warnings and service-selection classification, an explicit referral join and the full editable customer workspace. Its merged Operating Plans and declared-relationship operator extend the same source and customer workflow. The Directory chapter connects that delivered foundation to the existing source-specific T1 installation, T2 paid operation and T3 recurring-use/handover packages.

The Installation receiver-to-owner workflow also completed its full team-operated receiving: a receiver’s named observations return to the owner for explicit KEEP/APPLY decisions, changed criteria require a fresh review, and the next Installation edition remains editable. The original model/CLI, typed HTTP/MCP, desktop and phone Page, independent receiving and cold reopen all completed at revision 3. This demonstrates the handover and correction mechanism that T1 authority/handover and T3 recovery will configure for the two future customer installations.

**Named-staff operating result.** The completed staff workflow operated six profiles, three work records and two example invoices through contribution, review, payment and correction. Fifteen desktop/mobile browser views completed without errors. The independently restored installation retained and verified all 421 source files, and reopened the original business history after a cold restart.

Tranche costs are **$11,400 / $11,400 / $15,200**. The allocation is **320 engineering hours + 80 technical integration/handover hours**: 96 + 24, 96 + 24, and 128 + 32 across T1–T3.

Bryce owns delivery, source/release decisions and tranche submissions. Each workorder assigns integration, merchant/source, independent buyer, receiving/support and acceptance responsibilities. One person may hold several delivery roles. Merchant and buyer adoption counts follow accountable external organizations or people, each counted once in its role across routes, hosts, agents and wallets. Two endpoints controlled by the project do not establish two independent facilitators. The eighteen team-operated development purchases and later team-funded rehearsals remain engineering evidence and contribute no independent-adoption purchases to the funded cohorts.

Receiving covers the original source selection, complete reports/data and backups, an independent restore, managed Stop/reopen, and a later-edition comparison on the same keys, fields and population. Genuine unchanged data remains unchanged.

The day-150 release includes the saved product plan and Runtime handoff, dependency/license inventory, installation/upgrade instructions, configuration references and customer-state receiving procedure. It identifies the host owner, maintainer, primary/backup responders, service-cost owner and care scope. Updates start from deployed source, preserve resource identity and buyer/state records, review route/schema/payment changes and drain admitted work before switching traffic. Rollback preserves later purchases and output; restore reconciles operations after the backup point. Compatibility changes and migration instructions return to the maintained component, with open support cases retained in the handover. The receiving engineer also receives the saved application inputs, untouched original files and continuing working copies, complete operating procedure and returned-work review, and the selected Collections customer package. These records connect the installation to the customer's complete task and preserve the original purchase and delivery identities.

The grant funds prospective Stellar-integrated development. Completed pre-award implementation, sales, general operations, purchase principal and network fees have separate funding. Existing compute is the starting resource; incremental service reserve and hosted Actions budget are **$0**. Each adaptation is assigned once to a funded package or separate commercial workshare. Completed reusable work is reconciled with the remaining estimate at award.

For an environmental installation selected by the grant, the original workorder allocates the **remaining** customer-source adapter and complete receiving join to T1, facilitator/payment deployment and operating recovery to T2, and recurring mainnet use plus independent maintenance to T3. The shipped profile, source preparer and completed pre-award code remain its starting product. Each selected phase records its original commercial plan, assigned engineer, funding source and acceptance owner before work is scheduled. If a commissioned scope and a funded package use the same improvement, the case assigns its delivery hours once and retains the resulting source for both workflows. The five proposed commercial workshares retain their own fees, milestones and delivery clocks. They add no hours or amount to the existing **400-hour /$38,000 /150-day** grant request.

A source change is assigned to one package and one selected installation requirement before it enters the estimate. A reusable fix belongs to the public component; customer data, signing material and private configuration stay with the deployment. Package completion includes the corresponding documentation and receiving changes so the next operator can use the delivered capability.

T1 proves the deployed source-to-payment-to-output path using an existing supported facilitator. Its receiving result identifies the selected Stellar network and asset, payer, recipient, exact atomic amount and successful native transaction, together with the approved request and complete customer output. T2 funds the second independent facilitator's registration and compatibility work and the separate seven-day recurring-use cohort. T1 commissioning purchases remain in their original period and do not replace the T2 cohort. Both stages fit the existing package hours and costs.

## Threat response and outcome measurement

T2 delivers a threat model, corresponding installed monitoring plan and material corrections. Each installation records its source edition, authority, network/facilitator, protected records, observable signals, thresholds, notification destinations and primary/backup responders. The assessment covers altered offers or approvals, wrong payment/output attribution, unauthorized access, interrupted fulfillment, missing observations and restoration of the wrong generation. Application-level observation covers source and delivery failures.

The two operated response cases retain financial and delivery states, unfinished work, notification/acknowledgment, response/recovery times and the resulting useful output. The receiving engineer reopens the same history after restart, including observation gaps. The implementation follows Stellar's [threat-modeling guidance](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/security-docs/threat-modeling) and [builder monitoring template](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/security-docs/monitoring/monitoring-template-builders).

A completed purchase requires **one distinct approved intent, an independently observed native transfer and complete useful output**. Transactions are deduplicated per network; assets and fees remain separate. A prepaid pass counts once when its first agreed operation produces accepted output, with later calls retained as usage. Every agreed page/file or order action must be accepted before the customer task completes: the 144-row HPD example contains two paid pages and one complete task. T1 commissioning purchases retain their original period and identities; reopening them does not count toward T2's separate seven-day cohort.

The original first attempt determines cohort membership. Settlement and accepted output must fall within the selected seven- or fourteen-day window; later observations keep their actual time. Attempted, complete, partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes remain visible. Two-facilitator comparisons hold service, schema, population and output constant.

Customer benefit compares the prior task, first installed execution and recurring use on equivalent source/output: active effort, corrections, elapsed time to accepted output and unresolved work. A stated-period labor calculation uses comparable hours saved and the customer's stated hourly value, less implementation and incremental provider, host, payment and support costs. Accepted milestones, actual collections and support effort remain alongside those inputs.

### Installed responsibility and response
The installation workorder records the responsible operator at each boundary. These responsibilities travel with the maintained service when its receiving engineer changes.

|Boundary|Responsible operator and working handover|
| --- | --- |
|Source, offer and fulfillment|The merchant selects the authorized source, publication and terms. Its operator retains the release history, full delivery result and original fulfillment/accounting case.|
|Approval, signing and aggregate spend|The buyer operator supplies the existing signer or trusted provider and spending policy. The handover preserves the approved request, reservation and original dispatch; secret references are configured through the receiving host’s existing custody.|
|Facilitator and network|The selected facilitator operator owns its signing capacity, fee policy and service operation. Our integration retains its actual supported metadata, network/RPC observations and original settlement result; a third-party provider keeps its own administrative boundary.|
|Observation, recovery and receiving|Each installation names primary and backup responders, the supported observation sources and notification/acknowledgment route. The receiving engineer obtains the selected release, protected state, complete files and the original open cases.|

The existing threat model supplies ten threat decisions and eight monitoring/response definitions. Deployment binds them to actual sources, numerical thresholds and responders inside the same T2 package. Process availability, provider readiness, financial outcome and full delivery remain separate observations. A transfer that settled before an interrupted response is recovered through its original entitlement or delivery session. An uncertain transfer is reconciled before any further financial action.

The acceptance report includes the actual installation coverage and unresolved findings with the two original recovery cases. Public grant reporting uses the outcome counts, timings and sanitized source/version references; request bodies, account credentials, customer files and populated response destinations remain in the operator’s protected workspace.

### Maintainable release and support handover
The day-150 handover gives each independent operator one source-versioned release, its saved product plan and original installed Runtime handoff, dependency and license inventory, installation and upgrade instructions, selected configuration references, and the original customer data/state receiving procedure. The product briefing identifies that same selected installation and its observed package versions; the complete plan and original receiving records carry the source and operating state. It also names the host owner, maintainer, primary and backup responder, service-cost owner and separately agreed care scope. These are deliverables of the existing rollout and recovery packages.

The installed grant reviewer can turn the selected native SF47 work packages into a named customer operating procedure. It carries the original package scope, price, hours, relative work window and completion measure into ordered, editable steps; selected toolkit commands retain their source and runtime declarations. The receiving engineer adds the installation-specific instructions, actual due dates and recorded results in Operating plans. Complete saved revisions and readable HTML or Markdown carry that working procedure to the next operator alongside the original planning file.

Updates begin from the deployed source and preserve the merchant’s public resource identity, buyer records and state directories outside the installed package. The operator reviews changed routes, schemas and payment terms, stages the replacement and drains admitted work before switching traffic. A rollback selects a retained release while preserving later purchases and fulfilled output. A receiving-host restore reconciles operations after the backup point before continuing unfinished work.

During funded delivery, dependency or protocol changes are assessed against the selected Stellar SDK, x402 wire format, token/account behavior and the installations that use them. Necessary compatibility corrections return to the maintained source with the affected operating example and migration instructions. The selected provider’s sponsored-fee declaration, authorization lifetime, accepted payment flow and transaction payload remain explicit parts of that compatibility review.

At handover, the maintainer receives known limitations, open support cases and the continuation procedure for each one. The installed release and usable customer output remain available for self-operation. Paid care is separately scoped around the actual hosting, response and upgrade responsibilities; the grant’s 400 hours and $38,000 fund the prospective six-package delivery described here.
